newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA TARGET VENABLES TO COACH NATIONAL TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA TARGET VENABLES TO COACH NATIONAL TEAM.

text.p: Soccer Australia have targeted former England coach Terry Venables as the man they want to coach the Australian national team, according to a newspaper report.

The first edition of Tuesday's Herald Sun in Melbourne said that Venables was "one of several high profile names on Soccer Australia's shopping list" and reported that Venables was very interested in the job. He had asked Australian officials for the names of all Australians playing professionally overseas.
A spokesman for Soccer Australia did not deny Venables was due to have an interview with Soccer Australia officials this week -- but did not confirm it either.
"For obvious reasons we have to retain confidentiality on this but I can confirm we are speaking to a number of overseas coaches -- as well as ones at home," he said.

"We believe we are offering one of the great jobs in world soccer. Whoever takes over as Australia's coach has, because of Australia's dominance of the Oceania group and our path to the World Cup finals in France, a superb chance of taking the team to the World Cup in 1998."
Venables, 53, was not immediatly available for comment on Monday.
Since quitting as England's coach after taking his country to the semifinals of the European championship last June, he has worked without a contract at English first division Portsmouth.
The newspaper said that Soccer Australia might appoint two coaches, one based at home and one overseas to monitor some of the 150 Australians now playing around the world.
The vacancy has arisen following the resignation of coach Eddie Thomson three weeks ago.
Raul Branco, who is Australia's Olympic coach is currently working as acting national manager and was in charge of the side who beat Tahiti 11-0 on aggregate to become Oceania champions.

The Herald Sun story said that Soccer Australia had also targeted Jack Charlton, the former Ireland manager, Kenny Dalglish, the former Liverpool and Blackburn manager and Johan Cruyff, the former Barcelona coach, for the position.
